title: Share one audio-library read between AuditionReadout and AssetSetPicker
body:
## Summary
useAudioSetLibrary is instantiated per consumer with no shared cache, so LISTEN mode plus a selected bound emitter reads the library twice, and every selection of another bound emitter reads it again.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioScenePainter/AuditionReadout.tsx:486 and src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioPropertyPanel/AssetSetPicker.tsx:131 each call useAudioSetLibrary, which runs useCRUD with a custom fetcher of two GETs (src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioPropertyPanel/useAudioSetLibrary.ts:50-53). useCRUD has no endpoint cache or in-flight dedupe (src/hooks/useCRUD.ts:67). The emitter panel is keyed by emitter id (src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioView/PainterTab.tsx:97), so each bound-emitter selection remounts AssetSetPicker and refetches. GET /api/audio-gen walks the audio directory with statSync per call (open backlog card, database-layer). Fixed = one shared library read per painter-tab mount (module-level promise cache or a context provider) with explicit invalidation after generation/import.

## Flow
- enter LISTEN, select a bound emitter -> 2 hook instances -> 4 GETs (2x /api/audio-gen, 2x /api/audio/import-result)
- click through N bound emitters -> +2N GETs
- fix: hoist the library into one provider/cache read by both consumers; invalidate on Sound Forge generation

## Expected impact
Fewer directory walks on the dev server while auditioning; binding status appears instantly on reselect. Risk: a stale cache after a new generation if invalidation is missed.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one library read instead of one per consumer and per selection
Before: LISTEN + bound emitter = 4 GETs; N bound-emitter selections = 2N extra GETs (code-read)
After: predicted 2 GETs total per painter-tab mount
Method: simulation - counted hook instances and the key={id} remount by reading the code; the fetch-count test was not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test with a fetch spy: mount PainterTab, enter LISTEN, select 3 bound emitters, count /api/audio-gen GETs (before 4+, target 1)

title: Painter gestures die when the pointer crosses an in-canvas overlay
body:
## Summary
The canvas ends every drag/resize/draw on svg mouseleave, and five absolutely positioned overlays sit above the svg inside the same container, so dragging a zone under the minimap or toolbar drops it mid-gesture.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioScenePainter/AudioScenePainter.tsx:111 wires onMouseLeave={handleMouseUp}. Toolbar (Toolbar.tsx:247, z-10), Minimap (Minimap.tsx:358, z-10), AuditionReadout (AuditionReadout.tsx:495, z-10), ZoomCluster (ZoomCluster.tsx:321, z-10) and the commit banner (AudioScenePainter.tsx:166, z-30) all overlay the z-0 svg, so passing over any of them fires mouseleave and commits/ends the gesture. canvas-graph/direct-manipulation: capture the pointer on drag start so the drag outlives the element; release in every exit path. Fixed = setPointerCapture (or window-level move/up listeners like the minimap drag already uses, useAudioScenePainter.ts minimap effect) for item drags, resize and draw.

## Flow
- select mode, drag a zone toward the top-right
- pointer enters the Minimap box -> svg mouseleave -> handleMouseUp -> gesture commits and ends
- pointer keeps moving -> zone no longer follows

## Expected impact
Designers can drag items anywhere on the canvas without the gesture letting go near chrome. Risk: a capture not released on an early return would swallow later pointer events.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - gestures survive crossing an overlay
Before: 5 of 5 in-canvas overlays end an active gesture on entry (code-read)
After: predicted 0 of 5
Method: simulation - jsdom has no hit testing, so the cross-overlay leave could not be reproduced as a gate this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Playwright probe: drag a zone across the minimap and assert it ends at the release point; or a jsdom test that fires mouseleave mid-drag then window mousemove and asserts the staged op keeps updating

title: Zones, emitters and their delete controls are unreachable by keyboard
body:
## Summary
The painter is role="application" with keyboard zoom only; zones and emitters cannot be focused or selected by keyboard, and the two SVG delete controls are <g onClick> with no role, tabIndex or key handler.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioScenePainter/AudioScenePainter.tsx:71-72 announces only +/-/0/F. Zone bodies (ZoneLayer.tsx data-zone-id rect/circle) and emitter bodies (EmitterLayer.tsx r=10 circle) have only onMouseDown. The delete controls (ZoneLayer.tsx zone-delete g, EmitterLayer.tsx emitter-delete g) have onMouseDown/onClick only. There is no Delete/Backspace binding for the selection and no arrow-key nudge. Fixed = roving focus over items, Enter selects, Delete removes the selection, arrows nudge through the same SceneOp buffer, delete controls get role=button + aria-label + tabIndex.

## Flow
- keyboard user tabs into the canvas
- no item receives focus; Delete does nothing
- fix: roving tabindex over zones/emitters, Delete -> deleteZone/deleteEmitter, arrows -> moveZone/moveEmitter ops

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can author a scene. Risk: key handlers colliding with the existing zoom shortcuts.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - keyboard parity with pointer editing
Before: 0 of 2 item kinds and 0 of 2 delete controls keyboard-reachable
After: predicted 2 of 2 and 2 of 2
Method: probe - counted focusable/role attributes in ZoneLayer/EmitterLayer; the behaviour change itself is L and unbuilt
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioScenePainter/AudioScenePainter.tsx:72  aria-label="... Keyboard: + and − zoom, 0 resets to 100%, F fits to content."
ZoneLayer.tsx / EmitterLayer.tsx delete <g>: onMouseDown + onClick only, no role/tabIndex/onKeyDown
instrument: jsdom test: count tabindex/role=button among zone/emitter bodies and delete controls (0 -> 4), plus keyDown Delete on a focused zone commits deleteZone

title: Remove the painter and panel callback write paths no production code uses
body:
## Summary
AudioScenePainter keeps a second write mode (onCommit / onUpdateZones / onUpdateEmitters) and both property panels keep an onCommit mode with their own buffer; the only production consumer (PainterTab) uses the shared buffer/record mode, so the second path exists only for tests and has already drifted (no pitch clamp).

## Description
Zero-consumer grep: onUpdateZones/onUpdateEmitters outside __tests__ hit only AudioScenePainter/ itself; src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioView/PainterTab.tsx:71 passes buffer=, and PainterTab.tsx:86-101 passes record= to both panels. The compat path is useAudioScenePainter.ts writeScene + ownBuffer and the panels' own useRecordCommit (src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioPropertyPanel/useRecordCommit.ts:70, applyPatch = {...base,...patch}). That applyPatch lacks the pitchMin<=pitchMax rule src/lib/audio-scene-ops.ts:73-80 enforces on the live path, so two implementations of one rule already disagree. The invariant-placement deviation (types.ts union not pinned by a negative test) is recorded separately and not restated. Fixed = drop the callback variants and migrate the 4 test files to a useSceneBuffer harness.

## Flow
- 4 test files (AudioScenePainter.test, painter-commit-buffer, property-panel-commit, emitter-asset-binding) render the callback mode
- migrate them to a buffer harness
- delete the PainterWrites callback arm, writeScene/ownBuffer, NO_COMMIT and the panels' own useRecordCommit

## Expected impact
One write path to reason about; the pitch rule cannot diverge again. Risk: test rewrites lose a pinned behaviour if migrated carelessly.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the scene write path
Before: 2 write paths (buffer, callback) across 3 components; pitch clamp implemented on 1 of 2
After: 1 path; rule in one place
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep run this round; deletion not attempted (M, 4 test files)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the zero-consumer grep re-run after deletion (0 hits) plus the 4 migrated test files green; add a pitch-clamp case to property-panel-commit before deleting

title: Coalesce reverb impulse rebuilds while the Decay slider is dragged in LISTEN
body:
## Summary
A custom zone's Decay slider stages an op per frame; while LISTEN is playing each frame changes decayTime and synthesises a new impulse of up to 4 s of stereo noise.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioScenePainter/useSceneAudition.ts sync() rebuilds the convolver buffer whenever decayTime changes (the wet-only case was fixed this round, 405b6413). The ZonePropertyPanel Decay slider (step 0.1) edits per frame through the shared buffer, so AuditionReadout's mix memo recomputes per frame. Fixed = rebuild at most once per window (trailing debounce on the IR build with a UI_TIMEOUTS value) while still applying the final decay.

## Flow
- custom zone, LISTEN playing, drag Decay 1.0 -> 3.0
- 20 slider frames -> 20 impulse builds + 20 convolver swaps
- fix: debounce the IR build, keep the last decay

## Expected impact
No clicking or main-thread stalls while tuning decay by ear. Risk: the heard decay lags the slider by the debounce.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - impulse builds per decay drag
Before: N decay frames -> N builds (code-read)
After: predicted 1-2 builds per drag
Method: simulation - the createBuffer counter in scene-audition.test.tsx can measure it; the debounce policy needs a timing decision
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioScenePainter/useSceneAudition.ts sync(): if (reverbKey !== g.reverbKey) { g.reverbKey = reverbKey; g.convolver.buffer = impulse(g.ctx, m.reverb.decayTime); }
instrument: extend the scene-audition.test.tsx createBuffer spy: 10 decay-only rerenders under fake timers -> count builds (before 10, target <=2)

title: Associate property-panel Field labels with their controls
body:
## Summary
Field and SliderField render a <label>/<span> with no htmlFor/id link, so clicking a label does not focus its control and the visible label is not the accessible-name source.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioPropertyPanel/controls.tsx:5 renders <label> without htmlFor; the wrapped inputs carry separate aria-labels (e.g. "Zone name"). SliderField uses a <span> label. src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioPropertyPanel/AssetSetPicker.tsx:146 has the same bare <label>. Commit c7628915 fixed this class in AudioCodeGenPanel. Fixed = useId in Field/SliderField with htmlFor/id on the control (or aria-labelledby), dropping duplicated aria-label strings.

## Flow
- click the "Name" label in the zone panel -> input not focused
- fix: Field generates an id and passes it to its single child control

## Expected impact
Larger click targets and one source of truth for control names. Risk: Field children are arbitrary nodes (chip grids), so only single-control Fields get the link.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - labels bound to controls
Before: 0 associated labels across Field (zone+emitter panels), SliderField (11 sliders) and AssetSetPicker
After: all single-control labels associated
Method: probe - counted label elements without htmlFor by reading the rendered components
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioPropertyPanel/controls.tsx:5  <label className="text-2xs uppercase ...">  (no htmlFor)
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioPropertyPanel/AssetSetPicker.tsx:146  <label className=...>Library Asset Set</label>
instrument: jsdom test: every label in the rendered panels has htmlFor resolving to an element (count before 0)

title: New zones cycle through the muted "no preset" grey as a zone color
body:
## Summary
New zone colors cycle Object.values(ZONE_COLORS), whose first slot is ZONE_COLORS.none = var(--text-muted), so the 1st, 11th, 21st drawn zone is painted the neutral grey that otherwise means "no reverb preset".

## Description
src/components/modules/content/audio/AudioScenePainter/useAudioScenePainter.ts handleMouseUp: newZone.color = Object.values(ZONE_COLORS)[n % 10]; ZONE_COLORS.none is var(--text-muted) (AudioScenePainter/constants.ts). Rendering of variable colors was fixed this round (f8d0233b); this card is the palette choice: the first zone of every scene reads as unconfigured and has the lowest contrast on bg-surface-deep. Fixed = cycle a dedicated new-zone palette of distinct accent hues without the neutral slot.

## Flow
- empty scene, draw a zone
- it is grey (the preset-none hue) while the 2nd zone is blue
- fix: NEW_ZONE_PALETTE without the neutral

## Expected impact
Every drawn zone is visually distinct from "unset". Risk: changes only the default color of new zones; stored zones unaffected.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - first drawn zone gets a distinct hue
Before: 1 of 10 palette slots is the neutral muted token
After: 0 of N
Method: probe - read the palette; contrast not measured
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: lib/contrast.ts ratio of each palette hue vs --surface-deep (neutral slot is the minimum), plus a unit test that no new-zone palette entry starts with var(
